content: It is critical for future research to include the surveillance of pre-treatment integrase resistance and to focus on optimizing drug resistance monitoring. This could involve incorporating pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) into WHO drug resistance surveys and establishing routine protocols for sample collection, testing, and sequencing for individuals who seroconvert while using PrEP, including those using long-acting cabotegravir (CAB-LA) as PrEP. The availability of assays capable of detecting acute HIV infection, such as HIV-antigen immunoassays, fourth-generation HIV antigen-antibody immunoassays, and nucleic acid testing (NAT), remains limited in lowand middle-income countries (LMICs) where CAB-LA might be offered. The clinical and public health utility of these assays and testing algorithms is not as well-documented as the use of nationally validated testing algorithms, which often rely on rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs). For oral PrEP, same-day initiation has been a key factor in improving access and uptake. However, the use of NAT, which may require referral to external laboratories, sample transportation, and processing time, could hinder same-day initiation of CAB-LA. Implementation research is needed to evaluate testing strategies, including testing frequency and assay formats, while considering the intended use. Additional research is required to address concerns about HIV testing, including the potential role of HIV self-testing in optimizing testing frequency and follow-up after discontinuation. Investigating the factors underlying breakthrough infections despite protective drug levels is also essential, as this could inform the development of additional strategies. Furthermore, given the limited cases of integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) resistance identified among individuals exposed to CAB-LA, further research is necessary to determine the levels and patterns of cross-resistance between CAB and dolutegravir (DTG). Oral PrEP has been delivered through various services, including those for sexually transmitted infections (STIs), sexual and reproductive health, antenatal and postnatal care, and primary healthcare, across diverse settings such as clinics, pharmacies, and community-based locations. Task-sharing among healthcare providers, including nurses and trained lay providers, has played an increasingly significant role in PrEP delivery. Differentiated PrEP delivery models support comprehensive, person-centered services tailored to the needs and preferences of individuals who could benefit from PrEP, thereby enhancing uptake, continuation, and effective use. To date, CAB-LA has only been implemented in trial settings. Implementation science is needed to assess the feasibility and effectiveness of offering CAB-LA as an option alongside other PrEP modalities and HIV prevention services in various settings and with different healthcare cadres. Concerns have been raised by PrEP providers that CAB-LA might lead to the re-medicalization of PrEP services, as many providers have experience delivering PrEP outside clinical settings, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. Research is needed to understand the perspectives and needs of providers implementing comprehensive PrEP services, including CAB-LA, and to evaluate potential regulatory restrictions that may limit the administration of CAB-LA injections by appropriately trained providers, including lay providers central to oral PrEP services. Implementation studies should explore strategies to optimize CAB-LA delivery alongside complementary services, such as contraceptive services and gender-affirming care, during the same clinic visit. Research may also evaluate different injection schedules and innovative service delivery models, such as at-home or in-clinic self-injection of CAB-LA and community-based delivery, to support acceptable, effective, and efficient services. Preliminary mathematical modeling results suggest that increasing the total number of PrEP users, whether through oral PrEP or CAB-LA, has the greatest impact on reducing HIV incidence. CAB-LA use itself has the potential to avert additional HIV infections. Models for sub-Saharan Africa indicate that CAB-LA could be cost-effective even at a higher price than oral PrEP. However, further research is needed to assess the population-level impact, costs, and cost-effectiveness of CAB-LA across different settings and populations. This research should incorporate data from CAB-LA efficacy trials and implementation studies to develop realistic models that inform programs on impact and cost-effectiveness. Current models have largely considered extreme scenarios of PrEP scale-up and switching to CAB-LA; more realistic assumptions are required. Additionally, no model has yet included a PrEP method mix that incorporates the dapivirine vaginal ring (DVR). Cost-effectiveness studies should also account for additional costs associated with CAB-LA, including those related to different HIV testing approaches and schedules. This guideline is being launched as a web-based product for dissemination and will include all evidence presented to the Guideline Development Group (GDG). It will be incorporated into periodic updates of the WHO consolidated guidelines on HIV. Updates will be based on regular scoping exercises of available evidence and country implementation experiences. WHO headquarters will collaborate with regional and country offices, national ministries of health, and implementing partners to plan for the dissemination, adaptation, and implementation of this new recommendation. Key dissemination steps include presenting the recommendations at international conferences, conducting workshops to support country adaptation, developing tools to assist countries in setting priorities for resource allocation, and conducting briefings and joint planning with international and national implementing partners. Data on uptake will be made available through the WHO country intelligence database, updated every six months to reflect changes in policy and implementation across LMICs and selected high-income countries.
